problem: Data charts: resolve('a bar chart of weekly minutes') and resolve('a calendar heatmap of the month') return UNDEFINED (closest component/meter @ 4.0, itself only a horizontal fill). No chart marks, scales, grid treatment or data-palette mapping exist in the pack, and the circular completion ring has no register answer either.
insufficiency: The identity exists to present 'a lot of different data. Be that facts and figures, charts and graphs' (tdc.org, quoted in docs/synthesis/leader/00-evidence-inventory.md section 2), and Marber reserves the city accent palettes 'for data & sections' (inventory addendum; tile). Yet the pack carries no chart entry: component/meter is a single determinate bar; nothing decides mark form, series colour or grid.
reuse_case: Any data-bearing surface - bar comparisons, matrix/calendar views, series charts. This is core to the system's stated purpose (data presentation), not demo-specific, and the Cadence build needed three chart forms immediately.
composition_check: Not composable: tokens alone (grey ramp + city accents) do not decide chart form; no mark/scale/axis/grid/legend rules exist anywhere in the pack; and the ring-vs-rectilinear geometry question itself needs a canon answer. One pattern entry is the smallest change versus per-chart components.

proposed.title: Data charts (rectilinear register)
proposed.source_evidence: 00-evidence-inventory.md section 2 (TDC data/charts/graphs quote) + addendum (city palettes 'for data/section use'); 01-gestalt.md 'Rectangles are the geometry' (lines 23-25, 69-74); token-set/colour; guideline/surfaces

body.geometry: rectilinear only - bar columns, matrix/calendar cells, ruled axes; no circular gauges or rings (rectangles are the geometry; the demo's completion ring was an app-spec extrapolation - completion readouts use the meter/readout family instead)
body.palette: Chicago-blue family and the city accent palettes carry data series (the documented data/section role); Economist Red is the single attention mark (today/target), never a series colour; London grey ramp for tracks and neutral fills
body.grid: hairline rules/gridlines (London 85) - rules do the separating; no zebra, no box grids, no shadows
body.typography: sans for numbers and labels (metadata register); serif for chart titles
body.in_character: newspaper furniture: rules, ordered columns, one red mark per chart

tests: chart markup uses no rounded or circular marks (geometry check)
series colours are drawn only from the city palettes, with red appearing at most as a single attention mark (token check)
chart numerals use the sans register (type check)
